blocks.task_summary: Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀^(π/3) sec^n x tan x dx via substitution u = sec x (or integration by inspection), obtaining the antiderivative (1/n) sec^n x and evaluating limits to yield (2^n − 1)/n.
method_path: Substitute u = sec x, du = sec x tan x dx
Evaluate at upper limit x = π/3: sec(π/3) = 2 → 2^n / n
Evaluate at lower limit x = 0: sec(0) = 1 → 1 / n
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Rewrite integrand as sec^(n−1) x · sec x tan x; recognise that the derivative of sec^n x is n sec^(n−1) x · sec x tan x; integrate by inspection to (1/n) sec^n x; evaluate limits to give (2^n − 1)/n.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (A1) u = sec x ⇒ du = sec x tan x dx; M1 attempts to express integral in terms of u; A1 ∫ u^(n−1) du; A1 antiderivative [u^n / n]; M1 correct substitution of limits; A1 (2^n − 1)/n. METHOD 2: (A1) ∫ sec^(n−1) x sec x tan x dx; (M1) applies integration by inspection; A2 (1/n) sec^n x; M1 correct substitution; A1 (2^n − 1)/n.
